summary: Rows that open to show the rows under them, in columns compared down — spend by agent and then by task, a budget by team and then by person. The WAI-ARIA treegrid, drawn as a Table.
useWhen: the records nest — a total and the parts it is made of — and each level has the same columns to compare
the reader starts from the totals and opens only the branch that matters
a TreeView would do but each row has figures beside its name — size, owner, cost

useInstead.when: the hierarchy has one column — names only
useInstead.why: a tree grid's header and columns are overhead with nothing to compare down them

useInstead.when: the rows are flat, with nothing under them
useInstead.why: a Table sorts, resizes, holds its header and first column, and needs no expand keys

useInstead.when: a row opens to show more about that one record — its payload, its log
useInstead.why: that is a TableRow's `detail`: one record's own content, where a tree grid opens more rows of the same kind

useInstead.when: the levels are sections of a page — groups of settings, a FAQ
useInstead.why: content under headings is not rows in columns

composition.note: Pass the rows as `items`, each with an `id` unique in the whole tree and its `children`; pass `columns`, each with a `header` and a `cell(item)`. The first column holds the tree — the indent and the chevron — and is the row's name, so make it the name. `align: 'end'` for figures. Open the path to what matters with `defaultExpandedKeys`.
composition.example: <TreeGrid aria-label="Spend by agent" items={spend} columns={[{ id: 'name', header: 'Agent', cell: (r) => r.name }, { id: 'cost', header: 'Cost', cell: (r) => r.cost, align: 'end' }]} defaultExpandedKeys={['support']} onAction={openAgent} />

compact.use: a long breakdown scanned by eye, where more rows on screen matter more than room

relaxed.use: a short breakdown where each row deserves attention

none.use: the default: rows are read and opened, and Enter or a press is `onAction`

single.use: one row is the subject of what is beside the grid — a detail panel, a chart

multiple.use: rows are picked for a bulk action; a Checkbox per row and a select-all in the header

columns.note: each column's `cell(item)` is the row's content in that column. The first column's cell names the row: keep it text, or give the item a `textValue`

renderEmptyState.note: shown in one row across every column when `items` is empty; the grid keeps its name and header

requires: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` — the grid's name, such as "Spend by agent"
a unique `id` on every item across the whole tree — expansion and selection are held by id
a first column whose cell is text, or a `textValue` on each item — it is the row's name and what typeahead matches
guarantees: a `<table>` with `role="treegrid"`: only open rows are rendered, flat, each with `aria-level`, `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` among its siblings, and `aria-expanded` only when it has rows under it

one tab stop: ↑ ↓ move between rows, and between cells in a column; → opens a closed row and, on an open one or a leaf, moves into its cells and across them; ← moves back out to the row, closes an open row, and on a closed one or a leaf moves to its parent; Home and End go to the first and last row; typing jumps to a row by its first column
each row is named by its first column's text alone — not the chevron's name with it
each parent's chevron is a button named "Expand" or "Collapse" and the row's name, in the user's locale, out of the tab order; a press opens the row and puts the grid's focus on it
`multiple` gives each row a Checkbox named "Select" and the row's name, and the header a "Select All" that is indeterminate when some rows are picked; a click on the drawn box changes it once
select-all is every row that can be selected, open or not, and `onSelectionChange` always gets a Set of ids
selection does not cascade: a parent is a row of its own
a disabled item cannot be selected; it can still be focused, opened and activated, so the rows under it stay reachable
every level indents by spacing/20 and a leaf keeps the chevron's width, so labels at one level line up; in right-to-left the indent is from the right, the chevron points left, and ← opens
the focus ring is drawn inside the focused row or cell; in forced colours a selected row is Highlight, and its ring, chevron and checked box take HighlightText
notes: It draws as a Table does — the same container, density, header, rules and selected tint — but it is not composed of TableRow and TableCell: the rows come from `items`, so the keyboard model can know the tree.
No sorting and no column resizing. Sort `items` yourself, within each level, before passing them; a tree whose levels need resizable columns is a Table's job once flattened.
Built on React Aria's tree-table state, which 3.50 ships as `UNSTABLE_useTreeGridState` behind a flag. TreeGrid turns the flag on; it gates that hook and nothing else.

antiPatterns.dont: a Table whose rows are indented by hand, with a chevron button in the first cell
antiPatterns.why: indentation is not structure: a screen reader hears a flat table with no levels, and the rows under a closed one are still there to land on

antiPatterns.dont: a Table of TableRows, each with a `detail` that holds another Table
antiPatterns.why: a nested table is a second grid with its own header and tab stop, and its columns do not line up with the parent's

antiPatterns.dont: ids that repeat under different parents — two "run-1" rows under two agents
antiPatterns.do: ids from the path or the record — "support/run-1", "run_4821"
antiPatterns.why: expansion and selection are held by id, so two rows with one id open and select together

antiPatterns.dont: a first column of icons or badges, with the name in the second
antiPatterns.why: the first column holds the tree and names the row; a row named by an icon is announced as nothing
